title: Simple Pendulum
description: A ball on a string swinging from a fixed pivot demonstrates periodic motion and the conversion between potential and kinetic energy.
physics_concept: Simple Harmonic Motion, Conservation of Energy

objects.label: Pivot Point
objects.education_note: The fixed anchor the string rotates around. It applies no net force on the system — it only constrains direction.

objects.label: Pendulum Bob
objects.education_note: The mass swinging at the end of the string. Its period depends only on string length and gravity — not mass.

objects.label: Floor
objects.education_note: Provides a reference surface. In a true pendulum the bob never reaches the floor.

links.label: Pendulum String
links.education_note: An inextensible string. The tension T = mg·cos(θ) + mv²/L. At the bottom of the swing, tension exceeds weight.

controls.label: String Length
controls.education_note: Period T = 2π√(L/g). Doubling L increases T by √2.

controls.label: Bob Mass (Density)
controls.education_note: Mass does not affect period for a simple pendulum (Galileo's insight).

controls.label: Gravity
controls.education_note: Moon gravity (-1.62) causes a noticeably slower swing. Try Jupiter (-24.8)!

controls.label: Air Damping
controls.education_note: Real pendulums lose energy to air drag. Higher damping = faster decay of swing amplitude.

educational_sequence.title: Observe the Period
educational_sequence.instruction: Watch the pendulum swing. Count how long one full back-and-forth takes.

educational_sequence.title: Change Gravity
educational_sequence.instruction: Reduce gravity to simulate the Moon (-1.62). How does the period change?

educational_sequence.title: Change String Length
educational_sequence.instruction: Double the string length. The period should increase by a factor of √2 ≈ 1.41.
